### Describe the bug

When returning both a concrete type and an anonymous type in a private method a false positive is shown.
It suggests changing the return type to the concrete type.



### Steps to reproduce

```
class ConcreteType
{
    private object GetNewConcreteTypeInstance(bool returnAnonymousObjectInstead)
    {
        if (returnAnonymousObjectInstead)
        {
            return new { };
        }
        return new ConcreteType();
    }
}
```

### Expected behavior

No suggestion to be shown.

### Actual behavior

**Diagnostic ID**: CA1859: `Change return type for improved performance`

### Is this a regression?

_No response_

### Are there any workarounds?

_No response_

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Assembly version for DispatchProxy shim is too low resulting in duplicate types for DispatchProxy
Issues.Body:
Create a new `netstandard2.1` library.
Add a reference to `<PackageReference Include="System.Reflection.DispatchProxy" Version="4.7.1" />`
Try to use `DispatchProxy`

Expected: 
`DispatchProxy` is resolved from `netstandard.dll`

Actual:
```
error CS0433: The type 'DispatchProxy' exists in both 'System.Reflection.DispatchProxy, Version=4.0.6.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' and 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51'
```


Build contains conflict message:
```
Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Choosing 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' because AssemblyVersion '4.0.6.0' is greater than '4.0.5.0'.
```

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Fix Generate Constructor crash when inspecting properties in referenced projects
Issues.Body:
Fixes dotnet/roslyn#82157.

Generate Constructor can inspect a getter-only property declared in a referenced project to determine whether it is a `NotImplementedException` stub. Previously, this check requested a semantic model from the calling project’s compilation for the property’s syntax tree, throwing `ArgumentException: SyntaxTree is not part of the compilation` and causing Visual Studio to disable the provider.

Check that accessor syntax trees belong to the supplied compilation before requesting semantic models. Properties outside that compilation are not treated as reusable stubs, allowing constructor generation to create a new field instead. Also restrict accessor analysis to the current syntax-tree group.

Issues.Body:
Now this is a rather interesting bug I've run into accidentally, so excuse me for not having a minimal repro, but complete information instead.

**Version Used**: 

```
.NET SDK:
 Version:           11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128
 Commit:            3551975be0
 Workload version:  11.0.100-rc.1.26458.5
 MSBuild version:   18.11.0-1.26425.128+3551975be

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     debian
 OS Version:  
 OS Platform: Linux
 RID:         linux-x64
 Base Path:   /usr/share/dotnet/sdk/11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128

.NET workloads installed:
Brak zainstalowanych obciążeń do wyświetlenia.
Skonfigurowano używanie workload sets podczas instalowania nowych manifestów.

Host:
  Version:      11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128
  Architecture: x64
  Commit:       3551975be0

.NET SDKs installed:
  11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 [/usr/share/dotnet/sdk]

.NET runtimes installed:
  Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 10.0.12 [/usr/share/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App]
  Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 [/usr/share/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App]
  Microsoft.NETCore.App 10.0.12 [/usr/share/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App]
  Microsoft.NETCore.App 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 [/usr/share/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App]
```

**Also** reproduced in GitHub CI using SDK `10.0.401` with all different combinations of OSes: Windows, Ubuntu and OS X.

**Steps to Reproduce**:

1. `git clone https://github.com/JustArchiNET/ArchiSteamFarm asf-test`
2. `cd asf-test`
3. `git checkout a39fb49b14d0ad8139588c0bf2882d523be8e744`
4. `dotnet build`

**Expected Behavior**:

Build finishes. On my machine (Ryzen 7 7800X3D), this should take around 50 seconds total.

**Actual Behavior**:

Build goes into infinite loop, I've killed it after 10 minutes on my machine, CI was compiling it for around 30 minutes before I decided to forcefully kill it: https://github.com/JustArchiNET/ArchiSteamFarm/actions/runs/38185312652

I have no clue what exactly causes it, but I can pinpoint it to this particular commit that triggered it:

- https://github.com/JustArchiNET/ArchiSteamFarm/commit/a39fb49b14d0ad8139588c0bf2882d523be8e744

And this one as a silly workaround:
- https://github.com/JustArchiNET/ArchiSteamFarm/commit/3326f179e0cc4125ace88fbdbf2f34386aa171d6

**Notes**

I didn't manage to extract a clean repro, therefore I'm linking a real OSS project with a faulty commit - feel free to analyze any part that interests you. From those worthy of mention, the project intentionally uses `<AnalysisMode>AllEnabledByDefault</AnalysisMode>`, so the default `-c Debug` configuration actually runs all analyzers.

As a side note, you can also do `dotnet build -c DebugFast` to confirm that the build actually works, even on a faulty commit - `DebugFast` disables analysis through `AllDisabledByDefault`.

Thanks in advance for looking into it.

Issues.Title: Handle stackalloc syntax in RemoveUnusedMembers analysis
Issues.Body:
Fixes #85934

## Summary

The RemoveUnusedMembers analyzer currently treats
OperationKind.None as an unsupported operation and bails out
from analysis of the containing type.

Since stackalloc currently surfaces as OperationKind.None,
IDE0051/IDE0052 diagnostics are not reported for any members
within the containing type.

This change special-cases stackalloc syntax and preserves
analysis of the containing type while maintaining the existing
unsupported-operation safeguards.

## Testing

Added regression coverage for types containing stackalloc and
verified IDE0051/IDE0052 diagnostics continue to be reported.

Issues.Title: Compiler crash (ArgumentOutOfRangeException 'position') emitting PDB for partial union whose case list is in a later file
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**:

- .NET SDK 10.0.401 (`LangVersion=preview`, `net10.0`)
- .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 (same result with `net10.0` and `net11.0`)

**Steps to Reproduce**:

Repro repository: https://github.com/Summpot/roslyn-union-ice-repro

1. Create a project with the following files:

   `Repro.csproj`
   ```xml
   <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
     <PropertyGroup>
       <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
       <LangVersion>preview</LangVersion>
       <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
     </PropertyGroup>
   </Project>
   ```

   `A_Partial.cs`
   ```csharp
   partial union U;
   ```

   `B_Partial.cs`
   ```csharp
   partial union U(int);
   ```

   `UnionGlue.cs` (only needed for `net10.0`; with `net11.0` this file can be removed and the crash still occurs)
   ```csharp
   namespace System.Runtime.CompilerServices;
   public sealed class UnionAttribute : Attribute;
   public interface IUnion { object? Value { get; } }
   ```

2. Run `dotnet build`.

Observations:

- `dotnet build -p:DebugType=none` succeeds. `Optimize=true` and `DebugType=embedded` still crash.
- Putting both partial declarations in a single file succeeds.
- File order matters: renaming `A_Partial.cs` to `Z_Partial.cs` (so the declaration with the case list comes first) succeeds.
- The crash depends on the length of the first file. In a variant where `B_Partial.cs` has leading padding so that the case type `int` ends at offset 50, padding `A_Partial.cs` to 49 bytes crashes and padding it to 50 bytes or more succeeds.

**Diagnostic Id**:

N/A (compiler process terminates; no diagnostic is reported)

**Expected Behavior**:

The project compiles successfully. Debug info for the synthesized union constructors points to the case types in `B_Partial.cs`.

**Actual Behavior**:

The compiler fails fast:

```
error : Process terminated.
error : System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: Specified argument was out of the range of valid values. (Parameter 'position')
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Text.SourceText.LineInfo.IndexOf(Int32 position)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Text.SourceText.LineInfo.GetLineFromPosition(Int32 position)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Text.TextLineCollection.GetLinePosition(Int32 position)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Syntax.CSharpLineDirectiveMap.TranslateSpanAndVisibility(SourceText sourceText, String treeFilePath, TextSpan span, Boolean& isHiddenPosition)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CodeGen.SequencePointList.FindFirstRealSequencePoint()
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CodeGen.SequencePointList.GetSequencePoints(DebugDocumentProvider documentProvider, ArrayBuilder`1 builder)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CodeGen.MethodBody.GetSequencePoints(SequencePointList sequencePoints, DebugDocumentProvider debugDocumentProvider)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CodeGen.MethodBody..ctor(...)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.MethodCompiler.GenerateMethodBody(...)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.MethodCompiler.CompileMethod(...)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.MethodCompiler.CompileNamedType(NamedTypeSymbol containingType)
   ...
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.ErrorReporting.FatalError.ReportAndPropagateUnlessCanceled(...)
   at System.Environment.FailFast(String, Exception)
```

**Additional notes**:

The crash appears to come from the sequence point added in `SynthesizedUnionCtor` (`BoundSequencePointWithSpan(F.Syntax, ..., Locations[0].SourceSpan)`): the span is from the case type in `B_Partial.cs`, while `F.Syntax` seems to be the union's first declaration in `A_Partial.cs`.

Issues.Title: IDE0065 fix (`csharp_using_directive_placement = outside_namespace`) changes what names bind to, and `dotnet format` applies it silently: CS0104, CS0118
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**:

- .NET SDK 10.0.401, `dotnet format` 10.0.401-servicing.26423.113+e34a38d2ae1fc26406a317517196e55c68ff83ab
- Compiler 5.9.0-1.26423.113
- Windows 11 x64
- No third-party analyzers or NuGet packages: only the SDK's built-in code-style rules

**Steps to Reproduce**:

1. Create these five files in an empty folder.

   `Repro.csproj`:

   ```xml
   <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
     <PropertyGroup>
       <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
       <ImplicitUsings>disable</ImplicitUsings>
     </PropertyGroup>
   </Project>
   ```

   `.editorconfig`:

   ```ini
   root = true

   [*.cs]
   csharp_using_directive_placement = outside_namespace
   dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0065.severity = warning
   ```

   `Library.cs`:

   ```csharp
   namespace Shop.Domain
   {
       public class Order { }
   }

   namespace Shop.Legacy
   {
       public class Order { }
   }

   namespace Lib.Finder
   {
       public class Finder { }
   }
   ```

   `Ambiguous.cs`:

   ```csharp
   using Shop.Legacy;

   namespace Shop.App
   {
       using Shop.Domain;

       public class Handler
       {
           public Order Create() => new Order();
       }
   }
   ```

   `NamespaceVsType.cs`:

   ```csharp
   namespace Tests.Finder
   {
       using Lib.Finder;

       public class FinderTests
       {
           public Finder Create() => new Finder();
       }
   }
   ```

2. `dotnet build`: builds cleanly, 0 warnings, 0 errors.
3. `dotnet format Repro.csproj`, then `dotnet build` again.

**Diagnostic Id**:

`IDE0065: Using directives must be placed outside of a namespace declaration`

**Expected Behavior**:

The code still compiles and means the same. Either the fixer leaves a using directive where it is when moving it would change what a name in the file binds to, or `dotnet format` doesn't apply a fix that may change meaning and reports the diagnostic as not fixed.

**Actual Behavior**:

`dotnet format` exits **0** and moves both using directives above their namespaces. The second build fails:

```
Ambiguous.cs(8,16): error CS0104: 'Order' is an ambiguous reference between 'Shop.Domain.Order' and 'Shop.Legacy.Order'
NamespaceVsType.cs(7,16): error CS0118: 'Finder' is a namespace but is used like a type
```

A using directive inside a namespace is searched before the enclosing namespaces and the compilation unit's usings. After the move:

- `Order` is found through two compilation-unit usings at the same level (CS0104);
- `Finder` is found as the namespace `Tests.Finder`, a member of the enclosing namespace `Tests`, before any using directive is consulted (CS0118).

The fixer already fully qualifies the moved directive's own name (`ExpandUsingDirectivesAsync`), but not the names elsewhere in the file that the directive brought into scope.

In the IDE, the code action carries the warning "Warning: Moving using directives may change code meaning." (`s_warningAnnotation` in `MisplacedUsingDirectivesCodeFixProvider`). `dotnet format` applies the fix without any warning, so the first sign of the problem is a broken build. Seen in real repos: dotnet/eShop (`CreateOrderDraftCommandHandler.cs`, CS0104 on `Order`) and Ocelot (`DownstreamRouteProviderFactoryTests.cs`, 7x CS0118 on `DownstreamRouteFinder`), both with `outside_namespace` and IDE0065 at warning.

**Suggestions**, either of these would help:

1. `dotnet format` (and Fix All in general) skips code actions whose changes carry a `WarningAnnotation`, and reports the diagnostic as not fixed. This is in line with #75122, where the suggested direction was that Code Cleanup shouldn't apply fixes that aren't marked safe.
2. The fixer checks binding: it moves a directive only if every name in the file binds to the same symbol afterwards (or qualifies the names that would change), and otherwise leaves the directive in place.

**Related**:

- https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/75961 (closed): the same fixer broke an alias target's qualification. This report is about names elsewhere in the file, which the fix for that issue doesn't cover.
- https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/75122 (closed): Code Cleanup applied a fix marked "may change code meaning" and broke the code.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "IDE0065 fix (`csharp_using_directive_placement = outside_namespace`) changes what names bind to, and `dotnet format` applies it silently: CS0104, CS0118" (#86002)

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Restore localized first-run messages in the NativeAOT CLI
Issues.Body:
Backport of dotnet/sdk#55781 to `release/11.0.1xx`.

Cherry-picked squash commit `57066b1f1e885b1d84aa766c4b2a14def4500cc0` with `-x`.

## Validation

- Focused `dotnet-aot.Tests` regression: 2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- Clean `dotnet-aot` and `dotnet-aot.Tests` builds: succeeded with 0 warnings
- NativeAOT product publish (`win-x64`, Debug): succeeded
- Full Debug SDK build: succeeded with 0 warnings
- Focused redist-backed `dotnet.Tests` integration test: 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
## Tactics

### Summary

The .NET 11 NativeAOT CLI handled first-run setup itself, so the welcome, telemetry and certificate messages appeared in English on localized systems while later command output was localized. The fix (backport of #55781, fixing #55744) detects the effective UI culture, including CLI language overrides, in `NativeEntryPoint.cs`. For non-English first runs it defers to the managed CLI before any sentinel or setup state is written. English and subsequent runs keep the NativeAOT fast path. The change is small and targeted, so it suits servicing.

### Customer Impact

Users of the .NET 11 NativeAOT `dotnet` CLI on non-English systems (for example German Windows) see unlocalized first-run messages. The messages are displayed but in the wrong language. No workaround is stated in the PR. Only the first invocation is affected.

### Regression?

Yes. It affects the .NET 11 NativeAOT CLI, which printed first-run messages in English where the managed CLI localized them. The specific introducing PR is not identified in the available context.

### Testing

- New `NativeEntryPointTests` in `dotnet-aot.Tests` verify a German first run emits localized welcome and telemetry text. 2 tests passed.
- A new redist-backed `dotnet.Tests` integration test in `GivenThatTheUserIsRunningDotNetForTheFirstTime` passed.
- Clean `dotnet-aot` and test builds, the NativeAOT publish (win-x64, Debug) and the full Debug SDK build succeeded with 0 warnings.
- CI pipelines were started. Results are not reported in the PR.

### Risk

Low. The change is about 125 added lines across 6 files, mostly tests and design docs, with a 5-line change in the entry point and some build-props additions. It only affects first-run routing for non-English cultures. The English fast path is unchanged. The main edge case is culture detection, which the tests cover.

Issues.Title: Shorten paths in Full Framework tests
Issues.Body:
🤖 This is part of the weekly test issue cleanup effort.

Two Full Framework test scenarios can exceed Windows `MAX_PATH` on Helix because their generated test directories repeat long test and project names. This change gives those scenarios intentionally short, still-descriptive destination names:

- The packaged-command fallback test uses an explicit `Tool` destination, reducing the affected generated path by 20 characters.
- The RID warning test uses `NoFxRefs` for both its generated-project scope and project name, reducing the affected generated path by 42 characters.

Validation:
- Full SDK build (`build.cmd`)
- Both focused tests with the default test configuration
- Both focused tests with desktop MSBuild and a 181-character test execution root

Fixes #56498

Issues.Title: Use shared CI detection for MTP test output
Issues.Body:
`dotnet test` selected simplified ANSI output only for Azure Pipelines and GitHub Actions, although the SDK already detects additional CI providers. Reuse that shared detector and remove the fulfilled TODO referencing [microsoft/testfx#5533](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/issues/5533#issuecomment-2838893327); no testfx dependency update is needed.

The change preserves `--no-ansi` and LLM-mode precedence. Seventeen end-to-end cases cover all supported CI providers, local and false-valued environments, incomplete provider-variable pairs, and both output overrides. Each case isolates the spawned CLI's environment and verifies successful execution, test counts, and ANSI output without cursor-control sequences.

Fixes: #56595

## Validation

Built the baseline SDK with `build.cmd`, then rebuilt the changed CLI and deployed it into the `12.0.100-dev` redist SDK layout. Verified that the built and deployed `dotnet.dll` hashes match.

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~GivenDotnetTestOutput'
```

- Before the fix: 9 failed, 8 passed, 0 skipped; exit code 2. All failures were missing simplified ANSI output for previously undetected CI providers.
- After the fix: 17 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; exit code 0. Product and test builds completed with no warnings or errors.

TRX and binlog diagnostics are retained under `artifacts\log\test-runs\dotnet.Tests\20261012-121246-156428` (baseline) and `artifacts\log\test-runs\dotnet.Tests\20261012-121736-182512` (fixed).

@@ -88,11 +88,13 @@

```

## Local adaptation notes
The Microsoft.Testing.Platform terminal UI reporter, hard-forked into 'dotnet test'. testfx has since split TerminalTestReporter into partial files; the SDK keeps a single TerminalTestReporter.cs. Each upstream partial is tracked so any upstream reporter change pings the SDK to reconcile. Upstream includes the whole folder via a glob (TerminalReporterContract.props), so when testfx adds a partial it must be appended here by hand -- see microsoft/testfx#10390. Sources are append-only: the tracking issue marker keys on the source index. Reconciled through 45f54c96: retry/flaky and slowest-test summaries, per-outcome test-result visibility, skipped-count coloring, and descriptive exit-code summaries are ported. INTENTIONALLY NOT PORTED: (1) the coverage summary (TerminalTestReporter.Coverage.cs) -- it renders CoverageScopeSummary/TestCoverageThresholdMessage, which are in-process Microsoft.Testing.Platform message types with no representation in the 'dotnet test' IPC contract, so the orchestrator never receives the data; porting it requires a wire-protocol addition first. (2) In-process retry attribution (RetryAttemptProperty) and TerminalTestReporter.TestCompletedWithoutResult -- the SDK does not yet receive framework-level retry metadata and attributes retries per test-host instance id instead. (3) ShowRunSummary is never set to false by 'dotnet test': the SDK keeps one reporter for the whole execution and aggregates every attempt, so its summary already describes the whole run. This is a hard fork: local content intentionally diverges; the signal is 'upstream changed', not 'files differ'.

## How to reconcile
1. Review the upstream changes and decide whether they should be ported.
2. Port the relevant changes to `src/Cli/dotnet/Commands/Test/MTP/Terminal/TerminalTestReporter.cs`.
3. Update `eng/vendored-files.json` entry `dotnet-test-terminal-reporter` (source index 9):
   - bump `baseline_ref_sha` to the new upstream ref SHA,
   - bump `baseline_blob_sha` to the new upstream blob SHA.
4. Close this issue once the reconciliation PR is merged.

If no port is needed (e.g. whitespace-only upstream change), still bump the baseline SHAs to silence future runs.

Issues.Title: Skip unsupported Unix signing in SDK CI
Issues.Body:
**AI created PR**

Unix CI builds inherit `-sign` from `_CIBuild`, causing the pinned Arcade implementation to invoke Windows-only `sn.exe` for local strong-name signing even in dry-run mode.

Use explicit restore, build, pack and CI actions in both generic Unix pipeline commands, omitting the signing action. Windows signing, other build arguments and Arcade dependencies remain unchanged. This intentionally skips Unix signing validation rather than repairing SignTool; future `_CIBuild` action changes must also be considered for these Unix commands.

Removing `_SignArgs` alone, as in https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/55856, does not disable the signing action.

Validation: both YAML templates parse, and eight mocked build-script scenarios confirm `Sign=false` with all other emitted properties preserved. No full SDK build or affected Unix CI run has been performed.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56183

Issues.Title: `dotnet format whitespace` formats only the first target framework's `#if` code; `--verify-no-changes` passes while the build reports IDE0055
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

In a multi-targeted project, `dotnet format whitespace` only formats code that the **first** target framework in `<TargetFrameworks>` compiles. Code under `#if` for another target framework of the same project is never formatted, although the build compiles it and reports IDE0055 for it. `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` exits 0 on that code, so the tool and the build disagree about whether the project is formatted.

This is narrower than https://github.com/dotnet/format/issues/783, which asks to format code under `#if` symbols that *no* configuration defines (a feature request). Here the code belongs to one of the project's own target frameworks, and the build already reports it. A CI step running `--verify-no-changes` passes, and the IDE0055 warning from the build can't be fixed with `dotnet format`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create these three files in an empty folder.

   `Repro.csproj`:

   ```xml
   <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
     <PropertyGroup>
       <TargetFrameworks>net8.0;net10.0</TargetFrameworks>
     </PropertyGroup>
   </Project>
   ```

   `.editorconfig`:

   ```ini
   root = true

   [*.cs]
   dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0055.severity = warning
   ```

   `Code.cs` (both method bodies are indented by 10 spaces instead of 8):

   ```csharp
   namespace Repro;

   static class C
   {
       public static void A()
       {
             System.Console.WriteLine("A");
       }

   #if NET10_0_OR_GREATER
       public static void B()
       {
             System.Console.WriteLine("B");
       }
   #endif
   }
   ```

2. Run:

   ```
   dotnet format whitespace Repro.csproj
   dotnet format whitespace Repro.csproj --verify-no-changes
   dotnet build -p:EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true
   ```

### Expected behavior

- `A` and `B` are both reindented, since each is compiled by one of the project's target frameworks.
- `--verify-no-changes` agrees with the build: it either fails, or there is nothing left for the build to report.

### Actual behavior

- The first command reindents `A` only. `B` keeps its 10-space indentation.
- `--verify-no-changes` exits **0**.
- The build still reports, for net10.0 only:

  ```
  ...\Code.cs(12,6): warning IDE0055: Fix formatting (https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/code-analysis/style-rules/ide0055) [...\Repro.csproj::TargetFramework=net10.0]
  ```

With `<TargetFrameworks>net10.0;net8.0</TargetFrameworks>` it is the other way round: code under `#if !NET10_0_OR_GREATER` is skipped. So the whitespace pass formats each document as parsed by the first target framework only.

### Is this a regression?

Not known.

### Are there any workarounds?

- Run `dotnet format` once per target framework with `TargetFramework=<tfm>` set as an **environment variable**, so MSBuild loads each project as a single inner build. In a solution, this needs care for referenced projects that don't target that framework. A built-in option to pick the framework (https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/41899, also https://github.com/dotnet/format/issues/2057) would make this easier.
- `dotnet format style --diagnostics IDE0055 --severity warn` does fix `B` in this small repro, because each linked copy is analyzed. In larger multi-targeted projects, though, that path runs into the linked-file merge bug https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/86000 (conflict markers written into the source).

### dotnet --info output

```console
.NET SDK:
 Version:           10.0.401
 Commit:            e34a38d2ae
 MSBuild version:   18.9.11+e34a38d2a

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     Windows
 OS Version:  10.0.26300
 OS Platform: Windows
 RID:         win-x64

Host:
  Version:      10.0.12


`dotnet format --version`: 10.0.401-servicing.26423.113+e34a38d2ae1fc26406a317517196e55c68ff83ab
```

### IDE version

None (command line only).

### Other details

No third-party analyzers or NuGet packages; only the SDK's built-in IDE0055.

Related:

- https://github.com/dotnet/format/issues/783: format code under `#if` symbols no configuration defines (feature request).
- https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/41899 and https://github.com/dotnet/format/issues/2057: select one framework in multi-targeted projects.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Avoid redundant dataflow in security analyzers
Issues.Body:
> [!NOTE]
> This backport description was drafted with GitHub Copilot.

Backport of #56415 to `release/11.0.2xx`

Fixes #56413.

## Customer Impact

- [ ] Customer reported
- [x] Found internally

CA5390 and CA5403 spent substantial analyzer time processing thousands of literal byte-array call sites even when no relevant cryptographic sink was reachable. Issue #56413 documents a 2,048-call reproduction where the analyzers accounted for 42.179 and 10.426 seconds of a 53.97-second build. The source PR's targeted reproduction measured about 128 seconds before and 2.3–2.5 seconds after. This backport skips sink-free methods and runs taint analysis once per method, while retaining value-content analysis when source recognition or control-flow decisions require it.

## Regression

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

This is an analyzer performance optimization intended to preserve diagnostic behavior. Reachability checks account for implicit calls, initializers, branches, recursive helpers, and other cases that cannot be covered by a simple source-operation walk; ambiguous cases retain the full analysis. Regression tests cover these paths.

## Testing

The NetAnalyzers solution build succeeded with 0 warnings and 0 errors. Focused tests on `release/11.0.2xx` passed: 348 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed across the affected analyzer test classes.

## Risk

Production changes are limited to security-analyzer dataflow and property-set analysis; no public API or diagnostic ID changes. The implementation keeps conservative fallbacks where reachability or value mapping cannot be established safely.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Reduce CA1508 analysis cost for local-function calls
Issues.Body:
Backport of #56414 to `release/11.0.2xx`

Related to #56412.

No `servicing-approved` label is recorded on this PR yet.

## Customer Impact

- [ ] Customer reported
- [x] Found internally

In a project-scale reproduction, CA1508 accounted for 162.765 analyzer-seconds out of 187.173 aggregate core-project analyzer-seconds. Local-function calls repeatedly cloned and reanalyzed unrelated caller state, while nested functions could also be scanned as part of the enclosing method. This backport reduces that avoidable analyzer work for safe direct local-function calls and bounded static-local-function graphs.

## Regression

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

This is an analyzer performance change intended to preserve diagnostics. State is trimmed only when safe; uncertain indirect effects retain the full-state analysis. The backport adds deterministic coverage for local-function state, aliases, cached scans, and nested-function handling.

## Testing

The source PR's full CI passed. The release-branch pipeline for this backport is still running; release-branch test results are pending.

## Risk

The production change is limited to analyzer flow-state processing and CA1508 candidate scanning. It does not change public APIs or diagnostic rules. Conservative fallbacks preserve full analysis where trimming safety cannot be established.

Issues.Title: Emit CLI process identity as OpenTelemetry resource attributes
Issues.Body:
Process identity currently arrives only when the root command span ends, leaving telemetry from long-running commands uncorrelated to the OS process until exit.

- **Resource attributes:** Add numeric `process.pid` and `process.executable.name = "dotnet"` through shared resource configuration for tracing and metrics, used by both managed and Native AOT CLI builds.
- **Compatibility:** Preserve existing root-span attributes.
- **Regression coverage:** Assert both providers carry process identity while a child span exports before the root span ends.

- Fixes #56577

Issues.Title: dotnet watch crashes with NullReferenceException in AcceptChange after a failed project re-evaluation
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

`dotnet watch` crashes with an unhandled `NullReferenceException` (exit code 134) when re-evaluating a project fails and then any watched file changes. It should report the error and wait for a fix, and it does print `Fix the error to continue or press Ctrl+C to exit.` But the next file event kills it, and the app it started keeps running without it.

We hit this regularly in a real project. A script replaced the contents of an ASP.NET Core project's `wwwroot` while `dotnet watch` was running. The added files triggered a re-evaluation, that build failed because files were still being copied, and the next file event crashed the watcher.

### Steps to reproduce

Minimal repro: https://github.com/haagOS/dotnet-watch-nre-repro

```bash
git clone https://github.com/haagOS/dotnet-watch-nre-repro
cd dotnet-watch-nre-repro
./repro.sh
```

It is a console app whose `.csproj` has one extra target that fails the build while a file named `break-evaluation` exists. The script:

1. Starts `dotnet watch run`.
2. Creates `break-evaluation`. Adding a file makes `dotnet watch` re-evaluate the project, and that build fails. `dotnet watch` prints `Fix the error to continue or press Ctrl+C to exit.`
3. Deletes `break-evaluation`.

It reproduces every time (3 of 3 runs).

### Expected behavior

`dotnet watch` notices the change, re-evaluates the project, and continues.

### Actual behavior

`dotnet watch` exits with code 134:

```
dotnet watch ⌚ File added: ./break-evaluation
dotnet watch ⌚ Loading projects ...
dotnet watch ❌ Failed to build project '.../Repro.csproj'.
dotnet watch 🔨 .../Repro.csproj(13,5): error : break-evaluation exists: failing on purpose.
dotnet watch ⌚ Fix the error to continue or press Ctrl+C to exit.
Unhandled exception. System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
   at Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.HotReloadDotNetWatcher.AcceptChange(ChangedPath change, EvaluationResult evaluationResult)
   at Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.HotReloadDotNetWatcher.<>c__DisplayClass13_3.<WatchAsync>g__FileChangedCallback|1(ChangedPath change)
   at Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.FileWatcher.WatcherChangedHandler(Object sender, ChangedPath change)
   at Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.DirectoryWatcher.NotifyChange(String fullPath, ChangeKind kind)
   at Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.EventBasedDirectoryWatcher.WatcherDeletedHandler(Object sender, FileSystemEventArgs e)
   at System.IO.FileSystemWatcher.NotifyFileSystemEventArgs(WatcherChangeTypes changeType, ReadOnlySpan`1 name)
   at System.IO.FileSystemWatcher.RunningInstance.ProcessEvents(...)
   at System.IO.FileSystemWatcher.RunningInstance.<>c__DisplayClass14_0.<FileSystemEventCallback>b__0(Object o)
   at System.Threading.ExecutionContext.RunInternal(ExecutionContext executionContext, ContextCallback callback, Object state)
```

Any file event triggers the crash. In some runs the stack shows `WatcherAddedHandler` instead of `WatcherDeletedHandler`.

The app started by `dotnet watch` is not stopped and keeps running after `dotnet watch` exits.

**Cause, from reading the v10.0.401 source:**

- [`FileChangedCallback`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/v10.0.401/src/Dotnet.Watch/Watch/HotReload/HotReloadDotNetWatcher.cs#L216) captures the local `evaluationResult` and stays subscribed to `fileWatcher.OnFileChange` ([L226](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/v10.0.401/src/Dotnet.Watch/Watch/HotReload/HotReloadDotNetWatcher.cs#L226)).
- When a change requires re-evaluation, [L393](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/v10.0.401/src/Dotnet.Watch/Watch/HotReload/HotReloadDotNetWatcher.cs#L393) assigns the result of `TryEvaluateProjectGraphAsync` to that local. When evaluation fails, it becomes `null`, and the loop waits for the next change with the callback still subscribed.
- On the next file event, the callback passes `null` to [`AcceptChange`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/v10.0.401/src/Dotnet.Watch/Watch/HotReload/HotReloadDotNetWatcher.cs#L790), which reads `evaluationResult.Files`. The exception is thrown on a `FileSystemWatcher` thread pool callback, so it is unhandled and the process aborts.

The code is unchanged on `main`.

### Is this a regression?

Yes. It regressed in the 10.0.3xx feature band.

| SDK | Result (3 runs each) |
|---|---|
| 9.0.318 | No crash. `dotnet watch` reports the error and keeps running. |
| 10.0.100 | No crash. `dotnet watch` reports the error and keeps running. |
| 10.0.204 | No crash. `dotnet watch` reports the error and keeps running. |
| 10.0.300 | Crashes every time, same stack trace. |
| 10.0.401 | Crashes every time. |

Notes on the older runs:

- In every run that did not crash, the log shows the failed re-evaluation, `Fix the error to continue`, and then the delete event being processed normally.
- 9.0.318 and 10.0.100 print `Waiting for changes` only with `--verbose`, so the runs on older SDKs used `dotnet watch --verbose run` in the script.
- 9.0.318 re-evaluates through the `GenerateWatchList` target rather than a design-time compile, so for that run the marker target was also hooked `BeforeTargets="GenerateWatchList"`.

From the source: up to v10.0.204, a failed re-evaluation loops inside `EvaluateRootProjectAsync` until it succeeds, so `evaluationResult` is never `null`. From v10.0.300 on, `TryEvaluateProjectGraphAsync` returns `null` on failure and that is assigned to `evaluationResult`. That matches the runs above. The change came in #53466 (*Implements target framework selection for multi-targeted projects*).

### Are there any workarounds?

Avoid re-evaluation failures while `dotnet watch` runs. In our case, keeping the directory that gets rewritten out of what `dotnet watch` reacts to avoids it: adding `wwwroot/**` to `DefaultItemExcludes` only when `$(DotNetWatchBuild)` is `true`.

### dotnet --info output

```
.NET SDK:
 Version:           10.0.401
 Commit:            e34a38d2ae
 Workload version:  10.0.400-manifests.63b36e85
 MSBuild version:   18.9.11+e34a38d2a

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     Mac OS X
 OS Version:  26.7
 OS Platform: Darwin
 RID:         osx-arm64

Host:
  Version:      10.0.12
  Architecture: arm64
```

### IDE version

None: `dotnet watch run` from a terminal.

### Other details

Not tested on Linux or Windows; nothing in the cause is specific to macOS.

This issue was investigated and written up with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code).

Issues.Title: dotnet CLI: emit process.pid as an OTel resource attribute, not only on the root command span
Issues.Body: ### Summary The `dotnet` CLI's OpenTelemetry export records `process.pid` (and `process.executable.name`) as attributes on the root command span (e.g. `dotnet run`). Please emit them as **resource attributes** instead (or as well), so every signal from the process can be correlated to the OS process straight away. ### Problem OpenTelemetry only exports a span when it ends. For long-running commands (`dotnet run`, `dotnet watch`, `dotnet test` in watch mode, etc.) the root span lasts as long as the application does. For example, I observed a `dotnet run` span of 6m 2s, and that span only arrives after the command exits. Until then, the child spans (`telemetry-setup`, `parse`, `first-time-use`, ...) arrive with no process information. The only place the PID is recorded is the span that hasn't been exported yet. So while the CLI is running, there is no way to tell which process the telemetry belongs to, and by the time the span does arrive, the process is gone. Example `dotnet run` span (the only one that carries the PID): ```json {"name":"dotnet run","durationMs":4833, "attributes":{"process.pid":"52544","process.executable.name":"dotnet","cli.runtime":"managed","dotnet.globalJson":"valid","command.name":"dotnet run"}} ``` ### Why it matters Hosts that launch the CLI, such as .NET Aspire's AppHost (`dotnet run` per project resource), forward their `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` configuration to the child process, so the CLI's telemetry lands in the same collector or dashboard. Today it shows up as a separate `dotnet-cli-` resource with no link to the process or the resource that started it. See https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/20885. Knowing the PID up front would let tooling match the CLI's telemetry to the process it launched. The same applies to any collector that wants to tie CLI spans to a process. ### Proposal - Add `process.pid` to the OTel `Resource` for the CLI's tracer provider (and any metrics/logs providers), so it is sent on every export batch. - Consider also moving `process.executable.name` there. Both are process-level attributes: `process.*` attributes are modelled as resource attributes in the [OpenTelemetry process semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/resource/process/). - Optionally leave a copy on the command span for backwards compatibility. ### Environment - .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 - Windows 11
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "dotnet CLI: emit process.pid as an OTel resource attribute, not only on the root command span" (#56577)

Issues.Title: Recognize IsApplePlatform as a four-platform OS guard
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Teach the platform compatibility analyzer (CA1416) to recognize `OperatingSystem.IsApplePlatform()` as a guard for the union of these four platforms:

- macOS
- MacCatalyst
- iOS
- tvOS

This supports the public API introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/135475. The current runtime implementation does not include watchOS, and the analyzer follows that definition.

This change is entirely within the analyzer and its tests. It does not require changes to the runtime implementation, reference API, or platform guard attributes.

## Problem

The analyzer already discovers `OperatingSystem.IsApplePlatform()` through its existing convention for static, parameterless Boolean methods named `Is*` on `System.OperatingSystem`.

However, the existing decoder assumes that each such method represents one platform. It removes the `Is` prefix and therefore interprets this method as a check for a fictitious platform named `ApplePlatform`, rather than a check for four actual platforms.

This can produce both false positives and false negatives:

- **False positive:** an API supported on all four Apple platforms can still receive CA1416 inside an `IsApplePlatform()` guard because `ApplePlatform` does not match its supported platform annotations.
- **False negative:** an API annotated with `[UnsupportedOSPlatform("ios")]` can incorrectly have its warning suppressed because the fictitious `ApplePlatform` is treated as different from `ios`, even though the guard can be true on iOS.

Calls to APIs annotated only with `[UnsupportedOSPlatform("windows")]` can already appear to work with the old decoder. That result is coincidental: it does not demonstrate that the analyzer understands the Apple platform set.

## Implementation

Add an `IsApplePlatform` method-name constant and special-case this method in the parameterless branch of `PlatformMethodValue.TryDecode`, before the existing single-platform name extraction.

The decoder emits four unversioned, non-negated `PlatformMethodValue` instances:

```text
macos
maccatalyst
ios
tvos
```

The existing operation visitor merges these values with OR semantics. Existing control-flow analysis also handles negation, so neither the operation visitor nor the guard discovery logic needs to change.

The resulting behavior is:

- The true branch is reachable on any of the four Apple platforms.
- A guarded API must be safe on every reachable Apple platform, not merely one of them.
- The false branch, including an explicit `!IsApplePlatform()` condition, excludes all four Apple platforms.
- Windows and watchOS are not included in the true branch and are not excluded by the false branch.

The production changes are limited to:

- `PlatformCompatibilityAnalyzer.cs`: add the method-name constant.
- `PlatformCompatibilityAnalyzer.Value.cs`: decode the aggregate guard into four platform values.

`FilterPlatformCheckMethods` and `PlatformCompatibilityAnalyzer.OperationVisitor.cs` remain unchanged. No Unix platform-family mapping or OS-version behavior is introduced.

## Regression test setup

The existing test helpers use .NET 6 reference assemblies, which do not expose `OperatingSystem.IsApplePlatform()`. The new tests therefore provide a source stub with the exact `System.OperatingSystem` type name and a static, parameterless Boolean `IsApplePlatform` method.

The stub intentionally has **no platform guard attributes**. This ensures that the tests exercise the built-in guard discovery and decoding path changed by this PR, rather than the separate custom guard attribute path.

The method body throws `NotImplementedException`. Test source is compiled and analyzed, not executed; no runtime platform detection is involved.

The tests also explicitly configure:

```text
build_property._SupportedPlatformList = macos,maccatalyst,ios,tvos,watchos,windows
build_property.TargetFramework = net5.0
build_property.TargetFrameworkIdentifier = .NETCoreApp
build_property.TargetFrameworkVersion = v5.0
```

The target framework metadata enables platform analysis under the existing analyzer rules. `_SupportedPlatformList` ensures that the unsupported-platform annotations used by the tests are retained for analysis instead of being filtered out beforehand.

Including watchOS in this test configuration is intentional: it is a negative control that verifies watchOS is not part of the Apple guard. It does not add watchOS support to the runtime or the decoder.

Each `[|...|]` marker identifies a call that must produce CA1416. Calls without markers must remain free of unexpected diagnostics. The tests therefore check both required warnings and required suppression.

## Test coverage

Three test methods produce six executed test cases: one comprehensive C# case, four parameterized C# cases, and one Visual Basic case.

### 1. C# positive guard and implicit negation

`IsApplePlatform_GuardsOnlyFourApplePlatformsAsync` exercises both branches of:

```csharp
if (OperatingSystem.IsApplePlatform())
{
    // Reachable on macOS, MacCatalyst, iOS, or tvOS.
}
else
{
    // All four Apple platforms are excluded.
}
```

| API annotations | True branch | Else branch |
|---|---|---|
| Supported on all four Apple platforms | No warning | CA1416 |
| Supported on iOS and macOS, but not all four Apple platforms | CA1416 | Not exercised |
| Supported only on Windows | CA1416 | Not exercised |
| Supported only on watchOS | CA1416 | Not exercised |
| Unsupported on Windows | No warning | CA1416 |
| Unsupported on watchOS | No warning | CA1416 |
| Unsupported on iOS | CA1416 | No warning |
| Unsupported on all four Apple platforms | Not exercised | No warning |

These assertions cover:

- Correct suppression for APIs supported throughout the Apple platform set.
- Preservation of warnings when an API supports only part of that set.
- Preservation of an iOS deny-list warning inside the positive guard, preventing the original false negative.
- Exclusion of Windows and watchOS from the positive guard.
- Correct propagation of the inverse condition into `else`.
- Suppression of Apple deny-list warnings when all Apple platforms have been excluded.

### 2. C# explicit negation, independently for every Apple platform

`IsApplePlatform_NegatedGuardExcludesOnlyApplePlatformsAsync` runs with four data rows:

```text
macos
maccatalyst
ios
tvos
```

For each platform, it defines an API unsupported on that platform and checks:

| Condition | API unsupported on the selected Apple platform | API unsupported on Windows |
|---|---|---|
| `!OperatingSystem.IsApplePlatform()` | No warning | CA1416 |
| Else branch of that condition | CA1416 | No warning |

Testing each Apple platform independently verifies that all four values participate in decoding and negation. It also detects omissions from the platform set: a missing platform would no longer be correctly excluded by the negated guard.

Windows is an independent control that verifies the negative guard does not incorrectly exclude non-Apple platforms.

### 3. Visual Basic positive and negative guards

`IsApplePlatform_GuardsApplePlatforms_VisualBasicAsync` verifies the same built-in decoding path through Visual Basic operations and control flow.

| Condition | Scenario | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| `If OperatingSystem.IsApplePlatform() Then` | API supported on all four Apple platforms | No warning |
| Positive guard | API supported only on iOS | CA1416 |
| Positive guard | API unsupported on Windows | No warning |
| Positive guard | API unsupported on iOS | CA1416 |
| `If Not OperatingSystem.IsApplePlatform() Then` | API unsupported on iOS | No warning |
| Negative guard | API unsupported on Windows | CA1416 |
| Negative guard | API supported only on the four Apple platforms | CA1416 |

This covers both `If` and `Not` in VB and verifies that the fix is not limited to C# syntax.

## Validation

The new regressions were exercised against the original decoder and reproduced incorrect analysis involving the fictitious `ApplePlatform`. All six new cases pass with the fix.

The analyzer solution builds successfully with **0 warnings and 0 errors**:

```powershell
$env:DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH = '0'
.\build.cmd -projects src\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers.slnx -c Debug
```

The platform compatibility analyzer test group was run using the repository test driver:

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- `
    --project src\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers\tests\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers.UnitTests\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers.UnitTests.csproj `
    --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PlatformCompatabilityAnalyzerTests" `
    --skip-redist-check
```

Result: **344 total, 342 passed, 2 existing skipped tests, 0 failed**.

> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10569. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 1. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc1).

This is our first of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/dotnetmaui.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). Issues.Body: # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 – ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The IIS Middleware for ASP.NET Core did not properly constrain decompression of certain types of request, leading to excess memory consumption and a Denial of Service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69155 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** An out of bounds write can occur when processing PDB files. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/133437 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-122 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below Supported .NET Framework versions listed in the [Microsoft Security Update Guide](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-69522) are also affected. Install the September 2026 .NET Framework security update applicable to your Windows version. ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.10.0-beta1.24272.1, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 10 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 9 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET or Visual Studio. .NET Framework users must install the September 2026 security update applicable to their Windows version. 2. If your application references Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native, update the package reference to version 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 or later. Once you have installed the updated runtime, SDK, Visual Studio, or package, restart your apps for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Title: .NET 11 Preview 7
Issues.Body:
> This issue is a locked mirror of dotnet/core/discussions/10480. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Preview 7. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/preview7).

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-62900 | .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git and Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Improper removal of sensitive information before storage or transfer in .NET allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sourcelink/issues/1757 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-212: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transfer ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### Published NuGet packages Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 The affected packages used by .NET 8 and .NET 9 SDKs are built with SDK-specific prerelease versions that aren't published as stable NuGet packages. Update to SDK 8.0.130 or 8.0.424, SDK 9.0.120 or 9.0.317, or SDK 10.0.111 or 10.0.303 to receive the fix. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. A denial of service vulnerability exists in ASP.NET Core SignalR in .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. reconnect enabled. ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 10.0 Package name | Affected version |
